key_concepts: Cutting propagation uses a portion of a parent plant to develop roots and grow into a new
Healthy parent plants and clean, sharp tools improve cutting success.
Cuttings should include at least one leaf node.
Removing lower leaves and using rooting hormone can help cuttings root.
Cuttings need warm, bright conditions away from direct sunlight and regular watering.
Budding grafts a bud or small section of a desired plant onto a rootstock plant.
In budding, a T-shaped incision exposes the cambium layer for inserting the bud.
Proper alignment and contact between cambium layers are essential in budding.
Sterilizing budding tools helps prevent contamination and supports successful grafting.
Layering is another plant propagation method that uses a parent plant with flexible branch
